claim.why_it_matters: The rotated column headings of Table A.1 were transcribed with their words in reverse order (e.g. 'COUNT MESSAGE ACCEPT' for the ACCEPT MESSAGE COUNT statement, 'TERMINAL I-O INPUT DISABLE' for DISABLE INPUT I-O TERMINAL, 'value key Status' for Status key value). The headings no longer read as the statement forms they name; the X cells themselves match the PDF.

verdict.reasoning:
The 300-dpi render of printed page 665 (PDF page 687) shows Table A.1 with rotated column headings reading bottom-to-top: RECEIVE, SEND input-output-cd, SEND output-cd, PURGE, ACCEPT MESSAGE COUNT, ENABLE INPUT, ENABLE INPUT I-O TERMINAL, ENABLE OUTPUT, ENABLE INPUT, DISABLE INPUT I-O TERMINAL, DISABLE OUTPUT, Status key value. The page-687 markdown header row reverses the word order in every multi-word heading ('input-output-cd SEND', 'COUNT MESSAGE ACCEPT', 'TERMINAL I-O INPUT ENABLE', 'TERMINAL I-O INPUT DISABLE', 'OUTPUT DISABLE', 'value
key
Status'). Both sources are quoted accurately. The cause is that the rotated text was OCR'd in the wrong direction. This is more than formatting: the headings name statement forms (for example ACCEPT MESSAGE COUNT, DISABLE INPUT I-O TERMINAL), and in reversed order they no longer read as those statements. The column order and every X cell and status row match the PDF, so the defect is limited to the header text. The ninth column really is printed as ENABLE INPUT, the same as the sixth, so the claim reproduces the PDF correctly there.
